description: An auto-sampler: it plays a voice in the rack across a range of notes and velocities, records what comes back, and writes a folder of WAV files and an SFZ instrument to disk

params.text: Sets the lowest note of the sweep
Sets how many octaves the sweep covers, 1 to 8
Sets how many semitones apart the samples are: every semitone, every 2, every 3, every 4, every 6, or every octave
Sets how many velocity layers are captured per note, 1 to 4; at one there is no velocity switching in the result
Sets how long the gate is held for each capture, 0.1 to 10 seconds
Sets how long recording carries on after the gate releases, 0 to 10 seconds, which is what catches the release and any reverb tail
Starts the real capture on each press, after asking where to put the files; the readout shows the progress and then how many files were written
Runs the same sweep through the voice without recording or writing anything, which is how the sustain and tail settings are checked before a long capture

inputs.text: The left return from the voice being sampled
The right return from the voice being sampled

outputs.text: The pitch the voice is being played at, a volt per octave
The gate driving the voice, held for the sustain time, or a short pulse when the menu says so
The velocity the voice is being played at
A trigger when the sweep has finished and the files are written

notes: the module drives a voice rather than making sound: patch V/OCT and GATE into the voice and its output back into L and R before recording anything
the grid on the display is playable while the module is idle, so a patch can be auditioned note by note without starting a sweep; the display cannot be reached by clicking for help
menu: Set destination folder… — chooses where the WAV files and the SFZ file are written
Instrument name… — names the instrument, which names the folder and the SFZ file
Gate output — a label over the two choices below it
Gate (held) — holds the gate output high for the sustain time of each capture
Trigger (pulse) — sends a short pulse instead of a held gate, for a voice driven by triggers
Wait for silence between notes — holds off the next capture until the return has gone quiet, rather than moving straight on
Min gap between notes — sets the shortest pause between captures in milliseconds
Normalize — scales each captured sample up to full level before writing it
Auto-trim silence — cuts the silence off the front and back of each captured sample
Loop this instrument — marks the written regions as looping, for sustained instruments
Round-robin takes — captures each note and velocity more than once so a sampler can alternate between the takes
Channels: Mono, Stereo — writes one-channel or two-channel files
Bit depth — sets the bit depth of the written files, including a 32-bit floating point option
Calibrate latency — measures the round trip through the patched voice and offsets the captures by it, so the samples are not written with a delay at the front
Clear latency — throws away the measured round trip and records with no offset; it appears once a latency has been measured
Grid view — a label over the grid items below it
Layout: Chromatic (4ths), In-Key (scale), Chromatic grid (C0) — sets how the notes are laid out across the pad grid
Root — sets the root the In-Key layout is drawn from
Scale (In-Key) — sets the scale the In-Key layout is drawn from
Octave up — moves the pad grid an octave higher
Octave down — moves the pad grid an octave lower

outputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
